The original houses and other buildings of the Cumberland Homesteads community are characterized by the native "crab orchard" sandstone used in their construction. The federal government withdrew from the Cumberland Homesteads project in the 1940s. Federal planners envisioned Cumberland Homesteads as a model of cooperative living for the region's distressed farmers, coal miners, and factory workers. The Cumberland Homesteads community was added to the National Register of Historic Places as a historic district. The Cumberland Homesteads community survived after the federal government withdrew. Several hundred of the original houses and other buildings of the Cumberland Homesteads community were added to the National Register of Historic Places in 1988.
